units.title: Forecast: fresh breeze, a front later in the week
units.author: met
units.text: Marrow Sound, issued 06:00 ST. Today: southwesterly 4, occasionally 5 in the afternoon. Bright spells, a few showers in the north. Sea slight to moderate, swell about 1 m on east coasts. Max 9 C. Tonight: mainly dry, cloud increasing from the west late. Outlook: a vigorous front is expected in two days, bringing gales and a heavy swell to all coasts and islands. Small craft should take note.

units.title: Notice to mariners: emergency beacon, Kittering Holm
units.author: coast
units.text: Coastguard Marrow Sound. Late yesterday evening an emergency beacon registered to a site installation on Kittering Holm was activated. The Coastguard acknowledged the alert by radio. A coordinated response is being planned. Mariners are asked not to attempt a landing on the Holm, particularly after dark, and to report any lights, flares or signals seen from the water to the Coastguard on the usual channel. Further notices will follow.

units.title: Service update
units.author: ferry
units.text: Sound Lines. All sailings are operating to timetable today. We are aware of reports concerning Kittering Holm. The Coastguard has contacted us about vessel availability and we will publish anything relevant on this page. Please do not phone the Port Ammet terminal for information about the island: staff there do not have any, and the lines are needed for passengers.

units.title: Live: reports of a crew left on Kittering Holm
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 08:10 ST. We're following reports that Grieve Land Services, the contractor clearing Kittering Holm, has ended its contract and withdrawn its supply boat. Several listeners have told us people are still on the island. We have not confirmed that. The Coastguard has published a notice about an emergency beacon activated on the Holm late last night.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 10:05 ST. Correction: an earlier version of this page said the crew had been 'brought back to Port Ammet overnight'. That came from a caller and we can't stand it up. Grieve has not answered our calls this morning. We've removed the line and we're sorry for the confusion it caused.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 12:00 ST. The Coastguard tells Sound FM the beacon alert was received and acknowledged and that 'planning is under way'. Asked how many people are on the island, a spokesperson said they would not give numbers they could not verify. Figures circulating online this morning range from three to eight.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 14:15 ST. Sound Lines, which runs the Port Ammet to Lisle and Gilliver ferry, confirms the Coastguard has asked about available vessels. It says no decision has been made and that any crossing to the Holm would depend on the weather and on the state of the island's dock, which was built for the contractor's landing barge.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 17:00 ST. Still no statement from Ardent Vale Holdings, which owns the island. Its community information line plays a recorded message about 'stewardship of the Sound'. In Gilliver, people at the harbour told us the camp lights on the Holm were visible again last night, as they have been most of the month. We'll keep this page updated.

units.title: Holm clearance contract ends with questions over crew
units.author: courier
units.text: The contract to clear Kittering Holm of trees has ended without the clearance being completed, the Courier understands. Grieve Land Services, the land-clearing firm engaged by the island's owner, Ardent Vale Holdings, has withdrawn the supply boat that served its camp. It is not clear whether its site crew have left the island.

units.author: courier
units.text: Residents of Gilliver, which faces the Holm across nine kilometres of water, told the Courier they saw lights at the island's camp late last night. A creel fisherman who works the water off the Holm said the lights 'were on as usual, maybe brighter'. Another resident said she had 'never seen so many people on the front after dark'.

units.author: courier
units.text: The Coastguard confirmed it had received an emergency beacon alert from the island. Grieve did not respond to questions about how many workers it had engaged or how they were to be brought back to the mainland. Ardent Vale did not respond. The Courier will continue to ask, and will publish answers when it gets them.

units.title: Statement: contract KH-30 closed
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: Grieve Land Services payroll. Contract ref: KH-30 (Kittering Holm). Contract status: closed. Site day rate: ceased at the end of contract day 30. Final statement: pending reconciliation. You will receive a further notice when reconciliation is complete. Ref: PAY-KH30-CL. This is an automated message. Please do not reply to this address.

units.title: Long nights are here! Our lantern event continues
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Hello from Camp Supply! The nights are drawing in and our lantern event runs all week. Five tips for a cosy camp: keep spare batteries warm in an inside pocket, hang one lamp high and one low, check your wicks before dark, store fuel well away from bunks, and never leave a stove unattended. Free delivery on orders over $60 to mainland addresses. Happy camping!

units.title: Site
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi. I've been told the contract is closed and that I am not to contact site. I'm writing anyway, from home. This morning I gave the Coastguard the camp plan, the dock drawings and the radio details we hold. I don't know what head office has told anyone else, and I don't know what happens now. I'm sorry I can't give you more than that. Ruth

units.title: are you there
units.author: sam
units.text: it's on the radio. they're saying the company's gone and people might still be on the island and nobody will say who. I rang the number on your contract letter four times and got a recording about office hours. are you there? are you all right? I know you can't answer, you said the mail only goes one way out there, but I'm writing anyway. please be all right. love, S x

units.title: Not a joke this time, chief
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: No dad joke today, chief. I heard at the yard this afternoon. I've rung round everyone I know with a hull and a licence. Most of them said daylight only and only if the Coastguard says so, which is fair. One said no and put the phone down, which is also an answer. I'll keep at it. Keep your head down and keep warm.

units.title: Sorry to write again
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: I'm sorry, I know you're busy and I know none of this is your fault. Nobody will tell me who is still out there. If Tomas is with you, please tell him I'm fine. Tell him I've been round and fed his plant and it's doing better than when he left it. That's all. Sorry. Ana

units.author: sam
units.text: sorry, that last one was a mess. Mum doesn't know yet, I've told her the signal's down, which is true I suppose. the dog has been at the front door all evening, which he does anyway when the bins go out, so it doesn't mean anything. I'm going to ring the Coastguard in the morning and be very calm and very polite. love, S x

units.title: Gilliver tonight
units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: I might be wrong to write tonight, sorry. I walked down to the front at eleven. Every house on the harbour side has a lamp in the window, even the holiday lets, which someone must have let themselves into. Your camp lights were on. I counted them twice and got a different number each time, which is probably the distance. I don't know if that helps. Morrow

units.title: From the archive: a note on this week's requests
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note: we have had a number of requests this week for anything in the back issues about crews leaving the Holm. The nearest item is the village correspondent's column of February 1895 on the timber camp, which we will set out in full tomorrow. As always, the paper of the day did not check what it was told, and neither the camp's owners nor its men are quoted. G. Faulds

units.title: Penhallow camp ledger, winter 1894-95: the late entries
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Decr. 9th. Wind S.W., moderate. Felled and dragged 41 trees, the far lines idle. Wages paid to 22 men. Hanley and Tregear gone across on the boat with there tools and there pay, which I note was in full. Lamps lit at four by Mr Coad's order. No man to go past the second lamp on the yard path. Tally checked and correct.

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Decr. 11th. Hard frost. 33 trees. The men will not take the far lines now even in day light without three together, and I cannot fault them for it the days being so short. Nobody says why. Coad calls it idleness but dockt no one. Oil running low, the boat promised for the 14th. Psalm for the evening: the night shineth as the day.

units.title: Arnell notebook: Kittering Holm survey, final pages
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Day seven. Wind fresh. Ringed plover on the north shingle (Charadrius minor sonae, 2 pr.). Browse on the hazel heavy and quite untouched. Still no deer: no slots, no fewmets, no fraying on the birch. Boatman Creed asked again that we be off by four. I asked him why and he said 'tide', which it was not. (Sketch: a hazel stool, unbrowsed.)

units.title: Rendle diary, winter 1937-38
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Nov. 30. Wind W. Hauled 20 pots by the Holm side, 9 lobster, poor. Price at the quay down a penny. Mother lit the lamp at dusk same as always. Jory says the curing shed roof is gone at the Holm, he seen it from the boat. Never a sick man was sent there whatever they say in Ammet, it was all herring and salt.

units.title: Carrow Point log, middle watch extracts (winter 1906)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Jan. 4. 00:00 wind NE 3, vis. good, lamp burning well. 02:00 wind NE 3, light snow showers. 03:10 lamp trimmed. Remarks: two walkers on the shore road below the tower, standing, did not answer when hailed. Asst. keeper Rowe went to the gallery and could not see them from there. Logged here and not reported. E.S.

units.title: Rope Walk recycling. Again.
units.author: sb_bins
units.text: The council newsletter says, and I quote, 'collections are running as normal across the district'. Rope Walk's recycling sat at the kerb from six until it rained. As for the Holm business everyone is on about, it is none of our business, and I'd thank people not to park across the end of Rope Walk with their engines running while they ring the radio phone-in. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.title: Kittering Holm: contract ended, reports of crew still on the island.
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: This thread replaces the several new ones started overnight. Please keep it to what is known and say where it comes from. At present that is the Coastguard notice about a beacon, and Sound FM's live page. Speculation about named workers or their families will be removed without discussion. Their relatives may well be reading. Thank you. Pell.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Thank you, Pell. Worth separating three questions. Has the contract ended? Probably, given the supply boat. Are people still there? The beacon says someone was there late last night with power and a radio. Are they in danger? Nobody has said so. And what would we expect to see if they were all safely ashore in Port Ammet? Grieve saying so, loudly. It hasn't.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Just asking questions here, but why does a company with a supply boat and a contract with a very rich owner 'forget' its own workers? I said weeks ago this was a refuge for the rich and the crew were never part of the plan. Do your research on the dock. It was built for one boat, not two. Think about who the one boat is for.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Or a firm ran out of money and a few lads are camping on an island for an extra week. Grow up. Somebody will nip over with a rib and fetch them and they'll be in the pub by Sunday telling everyone about it.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Possibly, Cal, though 'somebody with a rib' is the part I'd question. The Holm dock faces east and there's a heavy swell due in two days. A small boat landing there in a lop is how you end up needing a second rescue. That's not drama, it's the tide tables and the forecast, both of which are free to read.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Practical question, sorry if it's the wrong place. My eldest came home from school saying the island workers have 'been left to die' because a boy in her class said so. I told her that's not what the radio said. Is there anywhere official I can point her to that isn't this forum? No offence meant to anyone here.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: None taken. The Coastguard notices page is the official source, and the council has said it will post anything relevant on its noticeboard. Sound FM's live page is careful and corrects itself when it gets something wrong, which is a good sign in a news page. Please don't send children here. Pell.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I have put a second lamp in the front window, the one that looks over the water. My mother woulld have done the same. It is only manners. I do not know who is out there and I would rather not be told names on here. I would rather just keep the lamps lit and the kettle on. Maud

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: I said on here weeks back I'd heard Grieve was 'paying well but you can't leave'. For the record I meant the contract terms, you couldn't walk off before day 30 without losing the lot. It was a moan about money off a lad in the yard at Port ammet. It wasn't meant like this and I feel sick reading it back.

units.author: fisher_bram

edit.text: Camp lights on again tonight from the Holm side, same place as all month, the yard and what I take for the cabin. Maybe brighter. I went out at five this morning, not four, clocks muddled in my head, and kept to my line. Nobody on the dock that I saw. Didn't go in. Not proud of that.

units.text: Camp lights on again tonight from the Holm side, same place as all month, the yard and what I take for the cabin. Maybe brighter. I went out at four this morning same as always and kept to my line. Nobody on the dock that I saw. Didn't go in. Not proud of that.

units.title: Ferries today (they ran, for the record).
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: The 07:10 was full of it this morning. Kerris was on and wouldn't be drawn, which tells you something, as she normally has an opinion about everything including my bag on the seat. The timetable ran fine. I mention that only because people at the terminal were asking whether the boats were being taken off for the Holm. They weren't, today.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Bernard, the Brackwater jct lights are stuck on red again so half of Port Ammet is cutting down Rope Walk to dodge them, that's your parking. Sat there twenty minutes at teatime with the radio on. Every bulletin was the Holm then the lights, the lights then the Holm. I know which one I'd rather they fixed.

units.title: Carrow Point station: daily summaries this week.
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Station summary for today. Pressure 1021 hPa and steady, wind SW 9 to 14 knots, max gust 22. Dew point 4 C, visibility 30 km plus, not a scrap of fog. Swell at the point about a metre and a quarter. The Met Office has a front in for the day after tomorrow and for once I agree with them. Readings into the night as usual.

units.title: Harbour notice: passages to Kittering Holm
units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Harbour notice, posted for information. Under byelaw 14 no vessel is to use the Gilliver slipway or harbour for a passage to Kittering Holm without notifying the harbour office, and the Coastguard has asked that no private landing be attempted. This is for everybody's safety, including the people on the island. Thank you for your patience with the phones. HM

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: For information. The company asked this afternoon which of the night crew would put their names down for a daylight relief sailing, if one is approved. I put mine down. That's all it is at present, a list with names on it. No vessel, no date, no plan I've seen. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Engine-room view: the relief boat is still on the slip at Weyhaven finishing her refit. The gearbox only went back in last week. She isn't going anywhere tomorrow whatever anyone on here hears. When she's back in the water I'd want two days of sea trials, minimum, and I'll be arguing for one, which tells you how I feel about it.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Mine's on the list too. I'm not saying more than that on here because the last time I said anything I got a fortnight of jokes about tall men in coats. Daylight, a proper vessel, a proper briefing, then yes. Anything less than that and I'm saying no, and so should anybody with sense.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: Lads. Shop phone has not stopped. I'm not organising anything and neither is anyone else off this board. Coastguard has it. If you've a boat and you want to help ring them and offer, they'll tell you yes or no. Nobody goes over there in the dark off the back of a forum post. Theories to the Sound Board.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Rang them. Offered the boat for daylight. They thanked me, took my number and said they'd want something bigger with a proper landing deck. Fair enough. Mine's twenty-six foot and the Holm dock was built for Grieve's barge, not for a creel boat with a dodgy winch.

units.title: Housekeeping: the island in the Marrow Sound
units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: a few of you have linked the Marrow Sound news about workers on an island. Those are real people with real families. Lamp Hours is company on the night shift, not a place to turn them into a campfire story. If you're local and know something verified, link the source. Otherwise please leave it be, have a glass of water, and tell us about your shift.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Port Ammet General here. Can confirm only that everyone on B corridor has heard, from the cleaners to the consultant. A&E has been told to expect 'possible casualties from an island' at some point, which is roughly what they're told about every boat that's late. Kettle's on, run's quiet, back to the trolleys.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Overnight producer, Sound FM. Agree with Ines. We had eleven calls about the Holm before midnight and I put two on air: a woman whose cousin works for the ferry, and a man who rang to say the island 'always takes its share', who I cut off. I watched three versions of one story move across the switchboard in an hour. Source? matters this week more than usual.

units.title: Kennel log, a quiet one
units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Quiet night so far. Twelve boarders, two post-op. Clover the old collie wouldn't eat until I sat on the floor with her, which is her right at fourteen. Back corridor update for those who ask: Moss still sits at the fire door and won't budge after two, so I walk him the front way. Not a mystery, just a dog with opinions.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Patrolled, nil found, which is my favourite kind of night. Respect to Moss. We have a guard dog on the east gate who won't go past container row K after midnight, and the handler says it's the reefer units humming. I believe the handler. I also walk row K with my torch on.

units.title: Rye night (and the second van)
units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Rye night, so the whole bakery smells like a wet field in the best way. The second van, the one that parks at the edge of the streetlight and never runs its engine, was back at three. I took a tray of seconds out to the kerb and knocked on the window. Empty cab. The tray was gone at four. I'd like to think someone hungry had it.

units.title: A request from the committee
units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Hello all. Some of you know that a friend of a resident on 4 has family on the island that's in the news. Please don't knock on doors asking for updates. If she wants to talk she will. The stairwell lights are still on, the lift is still slow, and the meeting about the bin store is moved to next week. Keep it kind. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: fair. for what it's worth nobody on 6 has been gossiping, we've mostly been sat in the kitchen refreshing the radio page like it's a train delay. it's weird when a news story is actual people. anyway the stairwell's fine, took the stairs tonight, no cardio of doom, just cardio.

units.title: Dawn chorus, reservoir north bank (daylight, before anyone asks)
units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Back with something boring on purpose. Dawn chorus from the reservoir north bank, 07:10 to 07:40 this morning, two omnis on a bar, handheld as backup, gain at minus 12. Robin, wren, a song thrush that wouldn't stop, a heron complaining about something. I'm doing daylight sessions only for a while. Make of it what you will.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so this is lovely and I'm really glad you're posting again. the thrush at about 14 minutes in does a phrase three times then changes it, which my year nines would call a loop. no arrows on the spectrogram this time, it's just birds. (typo fixed, I'd written 'phase' not 'phrase', obviously)
